tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Returns the signed-in user's profile: business name, address, saved payment instructions, whether their email is confirmed (required before sending invoices), whether they can take card payments, and client/invoice counts. Call this first to know who you are acting for.

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: Lists the user's clients (people or companies they invoice), optionally filtered by a search term matched against name, email and company. Use it to find a client_id before creating an invoice.

tools.name: create_client
tools.description: Creates a new client to invoice. Name and email are required; the email is where invoices are sent. Check list_clients first so you do not create duplicates.

tools.name: update_client
tools.description: Updates an existing client's details. Only the fields you pass are changed.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: Lists the user's invoices, newest first, without line items. Filter by status (draft, sent, paid), by client, or overdue_only for unpaid invoices past their due date (there is no 'overdue' status; use overdue_only). Use get_invoice for full detail.

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description: Returns one invoice with its line items, totals, status, the client it is for, a public_url the client can open, and a payment link if one exists.

tools.name: create_invoice
tools.description: Creates a draft invoice with line items for an existing client. Identify the client by client_id or client_email (must already exist; use create_client otherwise). Totals are computed server-side: subtotal + tax% + late_fee. Nothing is emailed until you call send_invoice. Returns the invoice, includ

tools.name: update_invoice
tools.description: Updates an invoice. Only fields you pass change. If you pass line_items, they REPLACE the existing line items entirely, so include every item that should remain. Works on draft and sent invoices; re-send with send_invoice if the client needs the new version.

tools.name: send_invoice
tools.description: Emails the invoice (with a PDF attached) to the client's email address and marks it as sent. This contacts a real person: confirm with the user before calling. Requires at least one line item and a confirmed user email. If the user takes card payments, a Stripe payment link is added first.

tools.name: mark_invoice_paid
tools.description: Marks an invoice as paid, for payments received outside InvoiceBloom (bank transfer, cash, cheque). Card payments through the payment link are recorded automatically.

tools.name: delete_invoice
tools.description: Permanently deletes an invoice and its line items. Cannot be undone. Confirm with the user before calling; prefer leaving paid invoices in place for their records.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_invoice" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Emails the invoice (with a PDF attached) to the client's email address and marks it as sent. This contacts a real person: confirm with the user before calling. …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account, list_clients, create_client · Private data: send_invoice, delete_invoice · Public sink: get_account, list_clients, create_client, update_invoice, send_invoice · Destructive: delete_invoice.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account, list_clients, create_client · Private data: send_invoice, delete_invoice · Public sink: get_account, list_clients, create_client, update_invoice, send_invoice · Destructive: delete_invoice

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
